Definition: A control that enforces network traffic policy across a trust boundary.
Intrusion Detection System -- an out-of-band monitoring technology that detects suspicious traffic but does not block it directly.
Intrusion Prevention System -- an inline control that inspects and blocks malicious traffic in real time.
Web Application Firewall -- a control that protects web applications by detecting and filtering malicious HTTP/HTTPS traffic.
A server-side intermediary that receives inbound requests on behalf of backend services.
A control point that authenticates, validates, meters, and logs API calls.
Network Access Control -- technology that evaluates endpoint identity or posture before granting network access.
The ability of an environment to restore business function after failure or compromise.
Increasing capacity by distributing workload across multiple systems.
Increasing capacity by adding more resources to a single system.
An architectural approach that denies implicit trust based on location and instead validates access continuously.
Reevaluating whether access remains justified throughout the life of a session.
Requiring stronger proof of identity when contextual risk changes.
The precise access relationship between a requester and a protected resource.
Fine-grained traffic control between individual workloads, services, or applications.
Moving away from sole reliance on a single network perimeter as the primary trust model.
Secure Access Service Edge -- a cloud-delivered architecture combining networking and security controls close to the user and workload.
Evidence that a device or workload is in a trustworthy state.
Marking data with visible or machine-readable indicators of sensitivity or handling requirements.
Applying metadata to resources or data so that automated controls can enforce policy.
Data Loss Prevention -- a set of controls designed to prevent sensitive data from being lost, exposed, or exfiltrated.
Layering controls so that the failure of one safeguard does not automatically produce compromise.
